rows.business_description:
Be It Enterprises LLC is a New York City M/WBE-certified community wellness company delivering wellness education, restorative fitness and movement, arts-in-health community engagement, and training and capacity building. We partner with government agencies, healthcare organizations, schools, faith-based institutions, senior centers, and community organizations to design and deliver culturally responsive programs that make health and wellness education accessible, engaging, and actionable.


Services include: 
wellness education and workshops; restorative fitness and movement; 

diabetes prevention and self-management education; community engagement; 

arts-in-health programming; Train-the-Trainer and workforce capacity-building programs; and customized community wellness initiatives.
________________________________________________________

Selected Experience & Collaborations:
• New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene — multi-site community wellness initiatives, fitness training and capacity building, and diabetes self-management education
• The Institute for Family Health / Bronx Health REACH — wellness programming, diabetes prevention, virtual fitness, wellness education, and Train-the-Trainer programming
• DISRUPT — community co-design and cancer health equity engagement utilizing Be It’s CRAVE® arts-in-health platform
• Mount Sinai — community health, wellness, and community-engagement initiatives
• Columbia University — community health and Community Health Worker training and capacity-building collaborations
_______________________________________________________

Signature Programs & Training:

BAFF® (Bed Aerobics Fitness Flow®) — We deliver wellness. Accessible restorative fitness and movement designed to support strength, mobility, flexibility, and confidence from supportive positions.

CRAVE® — We engage communities through arts and storytelling. An arts-in-health platform integrating performance, storytelling, health education, and community engagement to explore issues affecting health and strengthen community voice. CRAVE® is fiscally sponsored by the New York Foundation for the Arts (NYFA).

PACC (Physical Activity for Community Care) — We build the capacity of the people who serve communities. A participatory training workshop developed by Be It Enterprises to strengthen Community Health Workers' capacity to incorporate physical activity, wellness education, and practical movement strategies into community-based care.

Our Approach: Be It integrates education, movement, storytelling, and community engagement to support healthier behaviors, strengthen community participation, build community capacity, and advance health equity.

rows.business_description:
Since 1987, BERGFELD’s Clearance Services provides a full range of services to “de-clutter”, reorganize, “downsize” or liquidate personal property clients’ homes. We also specialize in helping people at risk because of hoarding.  

We have been instrumental in preventing several evictions of people at risk because of hoarding, many of whom have received a “Notice to Cure” or “Notice of Eviction”.  These contracts include actively collaborating with Landlords, Building Managers, Tenant/Landlord Attorneys and Legal Aid Community Services and Adult Protective Services (APS) of NYC Human Resources of Administration (HRA).  

As part of our clearance services for estate, moving or “downsizing”, we are pleased on behalf of our clients, to have donated truckloads of reusable possessions to charitable institutions such as Big Reuse, United Neighborhood Houses - New Settlement Community Center & Union Settlement, Bridge Builders Community Partnership - Children’s Village, Habitat for Humanity, City Opera Thrift Shop, Cathedral Community Cares (Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine), Vintage Thrift Shop (United Jewish Council of the East Side), Goodwill Industries, Cancer Care Thrift Shop and AFYA Foundation.

Among the Community Legal Services and Pro Bono Legal Services NYC we’ve work with are Mobilization for Justice, Goddard Riverside Law Project and Brooklyn Legal Aid. We’ve had clients in Assisted Living Residences such as St Margaret’s House and Atria West 86.  

BERGFELD’s has also collaborated with local elected officials and are honored to have received a Citation from NYS Senator Bryan A. Benjamin in 2018; a Proclamation from NYS Assembly member, Daniel O’Donnell in 2017.   Manhattan Borough President Gale A. Brewer (now NYC Council Representative for District #6) wrote us a letter of support in December, 2021 for our work helping people at risk because of hoarding and our prevention of evictions.  She has also forwarded our material to APS supporting our goal to enter into contract building on our WBE Certificate with APS in 2022.  This would be to collaborate and complement APS’ Heavy Duty Cleaning services.  BERGFELD’s plans to approach APS in early-February to discuss this.

Our goal moving forward is to actively collaborate with New York City Adult Protective Services (APS) and New York City Department for the Aging (DFTA) in support of services for the elderly especially helping people who hoard.  We will do this with our WBE Certification through NYC Small Business Services and seek renewal of our Certification.

Our services encompass new mobility consulting and program design, communications and curricula review, training and facilitation, community outreach and team-building activities.

We also acknowledge and adapt to traditional mobility vehicles that continue to play an integral role in urban mobility solutions. We specialize in light truck, automobile, traditional and electric bicycle and foot scooter education.

**Train the Trainer**: This capability ensures that our expertise and commitment to safety cascade effectively through the community and workforce, empowering trainers to carry forward our mission of creating safer and more accessible streets for all.

**Mobility Justice**: esm remains dedicated to advocating for fair and equitable transportation options, ensuring that traditional vehicle and public transit users are not left behind in our city's rapidly evolving urban landscape. We work collaboratively to eliminate disparities in access and promote safe and accessible transportation for all residents and workers.

At our core, we are more than just a content, training and education provider; we are the architects of a new methodology to teach safety and inclusivity through community building, innovation and empathy. Our mission is to educate and safeguard the well-being of every individual, from children to the elderly, and support the growing transport-dependent workforce.

Firm History

GdB (formerly known as Gayron de Bruin Land Surveying and Engineering, P.C.) was formed in 2010 by Christine Gayron, LS and Gregory J. de Bruin, LS, PE. In 2015 Jason Graf, LS became an owner. Every project is managed by a licensed professional. Equipment and software used include the following: Leica RTC360 Scanner, Leica ScanStation P20 Long Range 3D Terrestrial Laser Scanner, Leica and Sokkia Robotic Total Stations, Digital Levels with invar rods, Leica and TopCon GPS Systems, AutoCAD, MicroStation/InRoads, Civil 3D, Carlson Survey and Carlson Civil, Seafloor Hydrolite Echosounder system, ESRI ArcGIS. GdB specializes in production of plans employing as much customization and automation possible, the output being various agency CAD requirements. rows.business_description:
Jenn Miller Cribbs leads trainings and workshops that unlock the power of participants’ presence and voice, so they can advocate for their ideas with authority and facilitate productive dialogue in even the most charged circumstances. A nationally recognized expert in effective communication, Jenn has done this work with government agencies, corporations, nonprofits, community organizations, and schools, driving transformational initiatives of all sizes.

Jenn's work is rooted in the foundations of presence in our bodies, breath and voice. One half of that presence is the ability to be perceptive and responsive to what is actually happening around you. The other half is speaking and acting from a place of authenticity, in a way that is seen and heard by others as being authoritative, trustworthy, and open. This ability to be present is as primal as our survival instincts to fight, flee, or freeze, yet many of us remain stuck in a cycle of reactivity. When you learn to be truly present in conversation, it will unlock your ability to stay in dialogue and further the work you are seeking to do in the world, even with people with whom you profoundly disagree, revealing previously invisible paths forward in your work and relationships. 

Jenn is a Patsy Rodenburg Associate, and has worked closely with the legendary voice teacher for nearly 25 years, practicing her teachings on the foundations of presence in our bodies, breath, and voice. Her other influences include Resmaa Menakem, Iain McGilchrist, and Brene Brown. The tools and operating processes of Jenn’s trainings are based in her graduate work at the Columbia School of Social Work and her experience with Collective Impact models.
 
A member of SAG-AFTRA and AEA, Jenn has performed in theaters all over the country, played principal television and commercial roles, and served as a voice and Shakespeare coach on myriad productions and one-on-one with actors. Her performing arts experience grounds her teaching of presence and voice in warmups, techniques, and daily routines that result in the predictable ability to connect with one’s audience and draw them into conversation with the material and each other.
 
Jenn has a BA in Biology, Neuropsychology, and Communications from Wheaton College; an MFA in Acting and Directing from the University of Missouri-Kansas City; and a Masters in Social Enterprise Administration from the Columbia University School of Social Work. She was a Presidential Management Fellow, and won both the Rising Leader and Innovator of the Year Awards at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
 
Jenn lives with her husband and two daughters in Brooklyn, NY.
